newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end mixed, underperform on currency.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end mixed, underperform on currency.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended mixed on Monday, underperforming stronger U.S. Treasuries on a weaker currency, with the market focused on key U.S. inflation data due for released tomorrow, analysts said.

"With the Canadian market performance vis-a-vis the U.S., I think the currency probably had some play," said Craig Wright, deputy chief economist with Royal Bank of Canada. "That kept the bond market cautious."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.12 to C$116.46 to yield 6.716 percent.

The U.S. 30-year bond rose 14/32 to yield 6.69 percent. The spread between the bonds moved to three basis points from zero on Friday. On Thursday the Canada-U.S. 30-year spread traded negative for the first time in history.

Canadian bonds underperformed as the Canadian dollar ended weaker on Monday at C$1.3869 (US$0.7210) under pressure from heavy stop-loss selling. Dealers said many domestic players were caught trying to get out of long positions as orders to sell Canadian dollars drove the unit down.
Analysts said both bond and currency markets were focused on key Canadian and U.S. economic reports out tomorrow.

The key economic data out tomorrow include both the Canadian and U.S. consumer price index reports for May. The reports are expected to provide clues on the next likely interest rate moves by both the Bank of Canada and U.S. Federal Reserve.
"There are a number of key releases this week," said Wright. "I think there is some reason to be cautious as we move through the week."
Other major Canadian releases expected this week include the retail sales report for April out on Thursday.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.20 to C$108.22 to yield 6.133 percent, while the U.S. 10-year rose 7/32 to 6.40 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 27 basis points from 25 basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.85 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 4.96 percent.
